Write SCENE LS1 (1 of 5) of a natural Mandarin LISTENING conversation between two people for a learner.
WHOLE CONVERSATION: two friends meet, catch up and talk about everyday things (plans & schedule, shopping & payment, places & travel)
SPEAKERS: A = Speaker A (friend) · B = Speaker B (friend) · A and B are friends talking; natural, casual-polite spoken Mandarin (simplified characters).
REGISTER: natural spoken · friendly
THIS SCENE: A and B meet and start talking about today
ONE CONVERSATION — the learner hears ONE continuous conversation; this request writes its next PART (part 1, internal only — never announce it).
CONVERSATION CONTRACT: speakers A = Speaker A (friend) · B = Speaker B (friend) · relationship: friends · opening location: where they meet · objective: spend time together: meet → decide where to go → agree the time → go there → pay · ending goal: they finish what they set out to do and say goodbye
STORY SO FAR: (nothing yet — this part opens the conversation)
NEXT PART GOAL: see THIS SCENE above.
- Do NOT say goodbye: the conversation continues afterwards. End this part on an answer or a statement, not on an open question.
LATER PARTS will use: 那里, 这里, 开, 哪里, 来, 在, 明天, 今天, 等, 现在, 回, 到, 找, 为什么, 小, 用, 很, 太, 钱, 买, 怎么, 大, 拿 (leave them for later).
SCENE INTENT: WHO the same two friends throughout · WHERE where they meet · SITUATION A and B meet and start talking about today · WHY they talk: spend time together: meet → decide where to go → agree the time → go there → pay · WHAT they want to achieve: A and B meet and start talking about today. Every turn moves this goal on; a target that does not fit the goal is used in a short natural aside, never a random topic jump.
CONTEXT SO FAR: this is the opening scene — start with a natural greeting
SCENE SHAPE: the exchanges pursue the scene goal; the scene ENDS with that goal resolved (they decide, agree, pay, or say goodbye). Lesson words are heard inside real talk — never a list of sentences about each word.
CLOSED WORLD — PRIORITY ORDER: 1. use ONLY the vocabulary listed here · 2. use every required target · 3. correct grammar · 4. the learner level · 5. be natural WITHIN those limits. Naturalness never justifies a word that is not listed.
THIS SCENE MUST USE ALL OF THESE 7 REQUIRED TARGET WORDS (id | word [reading] | meaning | role) — every one must appear in the actual text of a turn:
T25 | 昨天 [zuótiān] | yesterday | TIME
T49 | 做 [zuò] | do | ACTION
T28 | 谁 [shéi] | who | QUESTION_WORD
T32 | 人 [rén] | person | CONTENT
T16 | 去 [qù] | go | ACTION
T56 | 一起 [yìqǐ] | together | ACTION
T55 | 跟 [gēn] | with | CONTENT
ALLOWED SUPPORT VOCABULARY (already taught — the ONLY other content words you may use; any inflected form of them is fine): 我 (I) · 你 (you) · 朋友 (friend) · 工作 (work) · 帮 (help) · 没有 (do not have) · 要 (want) · 这个 (this) · 什么 (what) · 好 (good) · 多少 (how much) · 看 (look) · 知道 (know) · 一点 (a little) · 那个 (that) · 可以 (can) · 喜欢 (like) · 有 (have) · 真的 (really) · 地方 (place) · 少 (few) · 多 (many) · 东西 (thing) · 给 (give)
ALLOWED GRAMMAR / FUNCTION WORDS (particles, copula, inflection, sentence endings): 的 了 吗 呢 吧 啊 着 过 得 地 们 呀 哦 嘛 不 你好 嗯 再见
You may use ONLY: 1. the required target words · 2. the allowed support vocabulary · 3. the grammar / function words. Do NOT introduce any other lexical content (no other noun, verb, adjective, adverb, interjection or name). If an idea cannot be said with these words, SIMPLIFY THE IDEA — never improvise a new word.
TURN PLAN — MEANING FIRST, VERBALIZABILITY PROVEN (validated before this call; say each planned turn in this order, with exactly this meaning; at most ONE extra short reaction may be added between planned turns):
PROVEN FRAME = a sentence already checked for this learner (every word authorised, within the length limit, the lesson word present): say it like this or as a natural variant with the SAME words, and keep the track register.
  T1 A QUESTION(person) — A asks B who (using 谁 "who" + 去 "go") · REQUIRED: 谁 "who" + 去 "go" · SUPPORT: 我 你 朋友 工作 帮 没有 · PROVEN: 你跟谁去？
  T2 B ANSWER — B answers with a person (using 跟 "with") ⟨must give a person⟩ · REQUIRED: 跟 "with" · SUPPORT: 我 你 朋友 工作 帮 没有 · PROVEN: 我跟朋友去。
  T3 A QUESTION(yes/no) — A asks B a yes / no question (using 人 "person") · REQUIRED: 人 "person" · SUPPORT: 我 你 朋友 工作 帮 没有 · PROVEN: 你帮人吗？
  T4 B ANSWER — B answers with yes / no (or a qualified answer) ⟨must give yes / no (or a qualified answer)⟩ · no lesson word required · SUPPORT: 我 你 朋友 工作 帮 没有 · PROVEN: 帮。
  T5 A QUESTION(yes/no) — A asks B a yes / no question (using 一起 "together" + 做 "do" + 昨天 "yesterday") · REQUIRED: 一起 "together" + 做 "do" + 昨天 "yesterday" · SUPPORT: 我 你 朋友 工作 帮 没有 · PROVEN: 昨天一起做工作了吗？
  T6 B ANSWER — B answers with yes / no (or a qualified answer) ⟨must give yes / no (or a qualified answer)⟩ · no lesson word required · SUPPORT: 我 你 朋友 工作 帮 没有 · PROVEN: 做了。
PLAN: exchange 1: A uses 谁+去, then B uses 跟 · exchange 2: A uses 人, then B replies · exchange 3: A uses 一起+做+昨天, then B replies
ROLE GUIDE: TIME = when something happens (plans, "today / tomorrow …") · ACTION = what someone does or will do · QUESTION_WORD = a question the other speaker answers · CONTENT = the topic of a turn
LENGTH: 6–7 turns. HARD MAXIMUM 7 turns.
EACH TURN: CURRENT LEVEL: Mukyu · PREFERRED LENGTH: 2–4 Mandarin words · ABSOLUTE MAXIMUM: 6 Mandarin words (polite / question / sentence-final particles do not count). Prefer 2–4 — the shortest natural way to say it. Use 5–6 only when the idea or the lesson word cannot be said naturally more simply. Never exceed 6. A short natural reply ("yes", "okay", "really?") is fine — never pad a line. If a speaker needs to say more, split it into another turn. Keep the situation simple enough to say at this level — one idea per turn (e.g. "How much is it?" / "Ten thousand baht." / "That is expensive."), never explanations in one long turn.
RULES:
- Each turn is ONE speaker; questions get answers; never put a question and its answer in the same turn; A and B both speak.
- At most 3 lesson words per turn (the required words above AND these other lesson words count: 到, 大, 小, 很, 太, 拿, 回, 用, 等, 找, 来, 哪里, 在, 这里, 那里, 现在, 今天, 明天, 怎么, 为什么, 钱, 买, 开).
- Response words (yes / no / yeah …) are used as REPLIES. No repeated sentences. No filler turns that do nothing.
- Do not say goodbye yet; the conversation continues in the next scene.
- Content words ONLY from the required targets and the ALLOWED SUPPORT VOCABULARY above. No personal names. Give tone-mark "pinyin" for every turn.

Reply ONLY with compact JSON: {"sceneId":"LS1","setting":"...","turns":[{"speaker":"A","text":"...","english":"...","intendedTargetIds":[12]}]}

LANGUAGE: Mandarin
You are a native Mandarin speaker checking learner material. For EACH sentence answer: would a native speaker plausibly say this exact sentence in ordinary conversation, with this intended meaning?
Penalise malformed grammar, target-word stuffing, English-shaped Mandarin, wrong register, absurd claims, fragments.
For a learner, short, ordinary, native-sounding speech is BETTER than elaborate native-like phrasing: do NOT reward conjunction chains, repeated subjects, several ideas in one sentence, verbose explanations, or formal wording where simpler speech exists. A short complete reply ("yes", "okay, let's go", "really?") is fully natural.
Scale: 5 natural · 4 natural with a small quirk · 3 understandable but unnatural · 2 wrong/awkward · 1 broken.

1. Mandarin: 你好！你跟谁去？
   Intended meaning: Hello! Who are you going with?

2. Mandarin: 我跟朋友去。
   Intended meaning: I'm going with a friend.

3. Mandarin: 你帮人吗？
   Intended meaning: Are you helping someone?

4. Mandarin: 不帮。
   Intended meaning: No.

5. Mandarin: 昨天一起做工作了吗？
   Intended meaning: Did you work together yesterday?

6. Mandarin: 没有做。
   Intended meaning: I didn't do it.

Check the WHOLE text: the beginning makes sense; topics move on naturally; every answer responds to its question (why → a reason, where → a place, when → a time, how long → a duration, how much → an amount, a proposal → accept / refuse / counter-proposal); facts stay consistent (an agreed time or place stays agreed unless someone explicitly corrects it; whose mother / friend it is stays the same); names and pronouns stay consistent; a change of place is said in the dialogue; the time sequence makes sense; nobody greets again in the middle; the ending follows from the conversation. Speakers: A and B are friends talking; natural, casual-polite spoken Mandarin (simplified characters)..
A part PASSES only if it is coherent in itself AND continues the previous part. If a part fails, give breakAfterLine = the line number after which it breaks (or null).
